label: History
value: Agatha Sowerby keeps a watchful eye over all travelers entering Brierley.
unit: Agatha Sowerby kept a watchful eye over all travelers entering or leaving Brierley from her kitchen window in Sowerby’s Hollow. In June, she observed Obed Abernethy dressed in his finest clothes and buggy, leading her to visit Thirza Abernethy at Grey Shutters, where she learned they were adopting an orphanage boy. When Obed brought home a red-haired girl named Nell Harcourt by mistake, Agatha voiced strong disapproval and misgivings. After suffering a severe bout of influenza, she visited Grey Shutters to inspect Nell, criticizing her freckles and red hair, which provoked Nell into a fiery rage. After Nell was disciplined, she offered a dramatic apology that completely won Agatha over. Over the following years, Agatha remained a central figure in Brierley’s community affairs, leading the Church Aid Society and evaluating new ministers, schoolteachers, and neighbors. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she cared for him devotedly until his quiet death. Following his passing, the farm was sold to pay a mortgage, and Agatha accepted Thirza’s invitation to move into Grey Shutters, establishing her own quarters in the former spare room and bringing her industrious nature and advice to the household.

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk is taken in as an orphan.
unit: Anthony Tulk is taken in as an orphan by Mrs. Laurence Tulk in Brierley and begins attending the local school. He quickly establishes a reputation for being cheeky and holding a strong prejudice against female teachers. During Nell Harcourt's tenure as teacher, Anthony continually shows open disrespect and insolence toward her. On a particularly stressful day, Anthony places a mouse in Nell's desk drawer; when confronted, he insolently admits to it, prompting Nell to lose her temper and give him a whipping with a hardwood pointer. Surprisingly, this punishment earns Anthony's respect, causing him to become polite, carry Nell's books, and defend her competence to others. He later joins the extra class preparing for the Regent's Entrance examination and successfully passes the entrance tests.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia's daughter married
unit: After her daughter married and left for the foreign mission field in India, Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house. Mabel Colby suggested that Aunt Euphemia move to Portmaris to act as housekeeper for her, Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay at Tabby's Place. She moved in during the autumn, bringing along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, as well as adopting the stray cat Smudge. She spent her days managing the household, knitting, and enjoying the lively company of the student boarders. When the girls departed for their summer vacations, Aunt Euphemia stayed behind at Tabby's Place to care for the house and cats. She remained to manage the house for a second year when the lease was extended.

label: History
value: Barney drove a double-seated buggy.
unit: Barney drove a double-seated buggy carrying Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and his sister Odette to and from a concert at the Pale Sands Hotel. He harbored a silent admiration for Nell Harcourt and frequently sought her proximity. Upon receiving the upper farm in his name from his father, he sought to take a wife. Too bashful to ask directly, he persuaded his sister Odette to propose to Nell on his behalf, offering to wait until she finished college. When Nell declined, he accepted her decision without heartbreak and married Nettie Scobie during the following summer.

unit: Belinda entered the service of Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage as a young girl, becoming the fourth in a line of Bowman sisters to be named 'Belinda' by her mistress. She quickly proved to be a loyal, hardworking, and affectionate handmaiden, assisting in the household and participating in Miss Rosalind's imaginative pursuits. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke visited Echo Cottage, Belinda welcomed them warmly and developed a deep admiration for Nell, attempting to imitate her graceful manners. She helped manage the household during Miss Rosalind's courtship and eventual marriage to Stephen Stanhope. Following their wedding, Belinda prepared to move to Boston with the newlyweds to continue serving Miss Rosalind.

label: History
value: Cedric arrives in Brierley
unit: Cedric arrives in Brierley from Boston to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope. On his first day at Brierley school, he instantly bonds with the new schoolteacher, Nell Harcourt, after sharing a silent, understanding smile with her. He soon becomes her favorite pupil and a close friend, frequently bringing her wild orchids and sharing his imaginative stories about 'rock people'. During a winter night when Posy Fay falls ill with croup, Cedric's quick action is not needed, but he continues to attend school diligently and bonds with his classmates, even engaging in a physical fight with St. Clair Trask to defend the honor of the American flag. Over the years, Cedric grows taller and becomes a protective figure for the younger schoolboys. When his father, Stephen Stanhope, visits Brierley and later marries Miss Rosalind Penrose, Cedric welcomes Rosalind warmly into his life. Following their wedding, Cedric prepares to return to Boston to live with his father and stepmother.

unit: Cedric arrives in Brierley from Boston to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope. On his first day at Brierley school, he instantly bonds with the new schoolteacher, Nell Harcourt, after sharing a silent, understanding smile with her. He soon becomes her favorite pupil and a close friend, frequently bringing her wild orchids and sharing his imaginative stories about 'rock people'. During a winter night when Posy Fay falls ill with croup, Cedric's quick action is not needed, but he continues to attend school diligently and bonds with his classmates, even engaging in a physical fight with St. Clair Trask to defend the honor of the American flag. Over the years, Cedric grows taller and becomes a protective figure for the younger schoolboys. When his father, Stephen Stanhope, visits Brierley and later marries Miss Rosalind Penrose, Cedric welcomes Rosalind warmly into his life. Following their wedding, Cedric prepares to return to Boston to live with his father and stepmother.

label: History
value: Cressida attends Wexcombe College as a Freshman.
unit: Cressida attends Wexcombe College as a Freshman, where she becomes close friends with Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis. She quickly becomes the beauty and social favorite of her class, attracting many suitors. During her second year, she rents Tabby's Place alongside Nell, Honora, and Mabel Colby under the housekeeping of Aunt Euphemia. While summering at Prospect Point, she meets Ezra Hale, an earnest theology student, and unexpectedly falls in love with him. In her Senior year at Wexcombe, she excels in Mathematics and earns the Johnson Scholarship. She eventually accepts Ezra Hale's proposal of marriage, agreeing to live a simple life as a minister's wife.

value: Cyril pauses his university studies
unit: After pausing his university studies to travel Europe with his mother, Cyril returns to Wexcombe College as a Junior. He meets Nell Harcourt when assisting her during a sudden rainstorm in the park, and soon begins courting her earnestly with gifts of flowers and poetry. Although his family initially holds reservations, Cyril remains devoted to Nell throughout his student years. Following graduation, he formally proposes to Nell at the park pavilion where they first met, but she realizes she does not truly love him and rejects his proposal. Though deeply hurt, Cyril accepts her decision and departs, eventually recovering and moving on as he had in past infatuations.

After attending Regent's Academy, she passed her Entrance examinations by a narrow margin. Later, she returned to Regent's for a second year rather than taking up teaching, as her family's wealth meant she did not need to earn a living. She participated in local events, including the Brierley school Christmas concert and B.V.I.S. meetings, though she frequently clashed with other girls and spread gossip.

label: History
value: Honora attended Regent's Academy
unit: Honora attended Regent's Academy with Nell Harcourt and her peers, excelling in her studies and forming close friendships. Afterwards, she taught at Delford school for a time before deciding to pursue her degree at Wexcombe College. During her time in Portmaris, she shared a home at Tabby's Place on Linden Avenue with Nell, Cressida Lindsay, Mabel Colby, and Aunt Euphemia. At Wexcombe, she studied hard, particularly in Classics, and participated actively in campus life and the Brierley Village Improvement Society. After completing her Senior year, she graduated with Honors in Classics alongside her close friends.

value: Hugh grew up in Brierley.

He taught at Pale Sands school after advancing to the fifth class and passing his entrance exams. Alongside Nell, he co-founded and led the Brierley Village Improvement Society to beautify the community. Hugh earned a First Class teaching license at Regent's Academy and won the academic Medal. Upon learning that Nell needed to stay near home, he selflessly withdrew his application for the Brierley school so she could be appointed, taking a teaching position at Pale Sands instead. After entering Wexcombe College, he became Freshman Class President and Captain of the Freshman football team, later earning High Honors in Classics and the prestigious Cooper Prize. He worked at the Daily News office in Portmaris to fund his studies, intending to become a doctor. After enduring a near-fatal bout of typhoid fever, he recovered and eventually proposed to Nell Harcourt in Dinah Wren's garden, gaining her love and a promise of marriage.

label: History
value: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill in Brierley.
unit: Isolde grows up at Pear Hill in Brierley and becomes the closest companion and bosom friend of Nell Harcourt shortly after Nell's arrival at Grey Shutters. The two girls swear a solemn promise of eternal friendship over a path they pretend to be flowing water, creating playhouses and sharing books. During a visit to her house, Isolde unintentionally becomes intoxicated after drinking three glasses of Thirza's currant wine, which Nell misidentified as raspberry cordial, prompting her mother to temporarily forbid Isolde from playing with Nell. This decision is later reversed after Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup. Isolde attends Brierley school alongside Nell, partaking in school activities, picnics, and a local concert performance. Later, when Nell accidentally falls through a roof while playing 'Elaine' in a flat-bottomed boat, Isolde helps rescue her. Though Isolde does not pursue higher education at Regent's or college, she maintains a close relationship with Nell through letters and visits. In her late teens, Isolde becomes courted by and engaged to Gideon Duckett, eventually marrying him in a home wedding at Pear Hill and giving birth to a son named Gideon.

label: History
value: After her mother's death, Lucy and Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy.
unit: After her mother's death, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy at Grey Shutters in Brierley. She adapted easily to her new home, helping with chores and keeping her clothes clean, in contrast to her twin. On one occasion, Robin tricked her into walking on a pigpen fence, causing her to fall in and ruin her clothes, after which he sprayed her with a hose to clean her. In September, she began attending Brierley School alongside Robin. Following the death of her uncle in British Columbia, money was left in trust for her and Robin, securing her future at Grey Shutters. Later, while playing, she accidentally fell down the exterior cellar stairs, stripping the skin off her nose, but recovered quickly.

In September, she began attending Brierley School alongside Robin. Following the death of her uncle in British Columbia, money was left in trust for her and Robin, securing her future at Grey Shutters. Later, while playing, she accidentally fell down the exterior cellar stairs, stripping the skin off her nose, but recovered quickly.

label: History
value: Mabel attended Regent's Academy.
unit: Mabel attended Regent's Academy, where she became close friends with Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis. After graduating, she taught for two years in an isolated rural school, where she grew exhausted by the demanding expectations of the community and students' parents. Tired of boarding and teaching, she decided to attend Wexcombe College to join the Sophomore class. She proposed that she, Nell, and Honora lease a small house in Portmaris called Tabby's Place, inviting her Aunt Euphemia to act as housekeeper. Along with Cressida Lindsay, the group lived together during their remaining university years. At Wexcombe, Mabel pursued her studies, took part in the Philomathic Society, and successfully completed her courses.

label: History
value: Nell Harcourt arrives at Alder River station.
unit: Arriving at Alder River station expecting to find a home, eleven-year-old orphan Nell Harcourt is met by Obed Abernethy, who brought her to Grey Shutters despite having requested a boy. Although Thirza Abernethy initially intends to send her back, Nell's emotional vulnerability and imaginative nature convince the siblings to keep her. She quickly adapts to Grey Shutters, making deep friendships with Isolde Pembroke and learning domestic skills under Thirza's firm guidance. When she enters Brierley School, an initial clash with classmate Hugh Carrow leads to a rivalry, though she eventually earns academic success. Over the years, Nell matures into an earnest student, leading the Brierley Village Improvement Society, founding a story-writing club, and successfully taking the Entrance Examination at the head of her class.

label: History
value: After graduating from Regent's Academy, Nell works as a teacher at Brierley School
unit: After graduating from Regent's Academy, Nell works as a teacher at Brierley School to help support Thirza and care for two orphaned twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. She implements non-violent discipline in her classroom and earns the respect of her pupils. When Obed Abernethy suddenly dies following the collapse of the Abbey Bank, Nell stays at Grey Shutters to comfort Thirza. Later, when a inheritance from Miss Lavinia Pembroke provides financial independence, Nell resumes her higher education at Wexcombe College alongside her friends. During her senior year at Wexcombe, she wins the Thorburn Scholarship in English and earns her Bachelor of Arts degree with High Honors. Following graduation, she returns to Brierley and reconciles her long-standing romantic feelings with Hugh Carrow, accepting his proposal of marriage as they look forward to their shared future.

label: Personality
value: Obed is extraordinarily timid.
unit: Obed is extraordinarily timid, bashful, and quiet, preferring to avoid unfamiliar people and women in particular, whom he fears might be quietly mocking him. He speaks very little and rarely offers details or opinions unless pressed, yet he possesses a deep, quiet stubbornness when he fixes his heart on something. He appreciates loquacious companions who handle conversation entirely on their own, and he shows immense gentleness, patience, and silent affection toward children.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy resides at Grey Shutters.
unit: Obed Abernethy resides at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza. Seeking farm assistance in his sixties, he and Thirza send word to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia. When Obed travels to Alder River to meet the train, he discovers that an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, has been brought by mistake. Though terrified of unfamiliar females, Obed enjoys Nell's lively chatter on the buggy ride home. Upon learning that Thirza intends to send her back, Obed quietly insists on keeping her, and Thirza ultimately relents.

label: History
value: Obed grows deeply attached to Nell.
unit: Obed grows deeply attached to Nell, continuously indulging her with gifts such as sweeties and a new dress with fashionable puffed sleeves, while secretly interceding to save her from harsh punishments. Over the following years, he works hard on the farm despite failing health and heart trouble. During a severe winter, he travels in the dead of night to secure a physician for a croup-afflicted child, proving instrumental in saving her life. When Nell wins the prestigious Avery scholarship, Obed is filled with immense pride. Shortly thereafter, he receives a letter announcing the sudden failure of the Abbey Bank, where his life savings are held; the shock triggers a fatal heart attack, and he passes away peacefully with a smile upon his face.

label: History
value: Flora Odette Tranter assisted her mother.
unit: Flora Odette Tranter (later Pullen) assisted her mother at Pale Sands Cove in taking in adopted children from Nova Scotia orphanages. She studied for her Regent's Academy entrance exams alongside Sukey and others, eventually moving to Brierley and attending the local school. She formed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, sharing in their childhood play and picnic adventures, though often providing a grounded, practical contrast to Nell's fantastical ideas. After graduating from Regent's, she became the schoolteacher at Stonebridge, earning a reputation for being strict yet dutiful. She participated actively in the Brierley Village Improvement Society, serving on various committees. Eventually, Odette gave up her teaching post to travel West, where she met and married Mr. Inglis, a wealthy mining man from Winnipeg. They later traveled to Europe on their honeymoon before settling into a grand mansion in Winnipeg.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer moved to Brierley.
unit: After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer quickly developed a reputation as a crank for his unusual domestic habits, keeping house without a woman and clashing with local busybodies. When Nell Harcourt's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed in his oat field, he flew into a rage and confronted her, but after Nell accidentally sold his cow instead of her own, the two reached an understanding, traded cows, and became good friends over tea and cake. During a severe thunderstorm, his parrot Nutmeg was killed when lightning struck the house, which deeply saddened him. Later, his estranged wife Emily arrived at Brierley after hearing false rumors that he was going to marry someone else. The two reconciled and resumed living together, with Emily taking over the housekeeping.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster of Brierley school
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster of Brierley school, securing the position largely because his uncle was a primary school trustee. During his tenure, he spent the majority of his effort focusing on older pupils preparing for Regent's, while showing romantic interest in student Sukey Pullen. He was known for making sarcastic remarks and handing out punishments, such as forcing Nell Harcourt to stand by the blackboard for breaking a slate over Hugh Carrow's head, or making her sit next to Hugh after she ran into class late. He also participated in the local Debating Club concert, giving an emotional recitation of Mark Antony's address. After the school year ended, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to his pupils and departed Brierley.

label: History
value: Ezra attended Wexcombe College
unit: Ezra attended Wexcombe College and studied theology at St. Columbia. During a summer break, he took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church, lodging at Cousin Emily's boardinghouse where he met Cressida Lindsay. He initially struggled with his religious calling but ultimately embraced it fully. After completing his theological studies at St. Columbia, he took over a small mission church in the Tanner Street slums. He proposed to Cressida Lindsay, and the two were married the following June.

label: History
value: Robin and Lucy are brought to Grey Shutters
unit: Following his mother Mary's terminal illness, Robin and his twin sister Lucy are brought to Grey Shutters to be raised by Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt. Upon arriving, he demonstrates an energetic, restless nature, quickly becoming fond of Nell while constantly getting into scrapes. Over time, he causes various domestic disruptions, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, pushing Lucy into a pigpen, placing a toad in Thirza's bed, and consuming restricted jam. He enters Brierley school alongside Lucy, where he competes in growth and antics with his classmate Milty Gammon. After his mother passes away and his uncle dies in British Columbia, a bequest secures money for his care. As he grows older, he continues living at Grey Shutters under Thirza's and Mrs. Agatha Sowerby's watch while remaining devoted to Nell.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy lived a quiet life
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived a quiet life at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her brother Obed. Expecting an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to help on the farm, they were surprised when an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, arrived instead due to a mix-up. Though Thirza initially planned to return Nell, she decided to keep her out of compassion and a desire to give her a proper Christian upbringing. Over the years, Thirza strictly raised Nell, teaching her domestic skills and moral behavior while coming to love her as her own child. When her brother Obed died suddenly following a bank failure, Thirza was left devastated and faced financial ruin. Her deteriorating eyesight threatened her independence, making her consider selling Grey Shutters, but Nell gave up her college scholarship to stay home, teach school, and care for Thirza. Eventually, Thirza invited her lifelong friend, Mrs. Agatha Sowerby, to live with her at Grey Shutters, enabling Nell to finally attend Wexcombe College.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne arrived in Brierley
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne arrived in Brierley as its first female teacher, taking over the school from Mr. Pidgeon. She quickly earned the deep affection of her students through her refined manners, field afternoons, recitations, physical culture routines, and essay assignments. When a job offer came from her home district, she decided to stay in Brierley to guide her students through their Regent's Entrance examinations. She established an extra after-school class to prepare advanced students, including Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow, leading them through rigorous drills and examinations until they successfully passed the Entrance. Afterwards, she concluded her teaching tenure at Brierley to accept a position elsewhere.

value: Miss Agnes Thorne concluded her teaching tenure at Brierley.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne arrived in Brierley as its first female teacher, taking over the school from Mr. Pidgeon. She quickly earned the deep affection of her students through her refined manners, field afternoons, recitations, physical culture routines, and essay assignments. When a job offer came from her home district, she decided to stay in Brierley to guide her students through their Regent's Entrance examinations. She established an extra after-school class to prepare advanced students, including Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow, leading them through rigorous drills and examinations until they successfully passed the Entrance. Afterwards, she concluded her teaching tenure at Brierley to accept a position elsewhere.
